chunks: Sahl, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the man is cut in the middle into two halves, Salat (prayer) would be prayed upon that in which is the heart.

key_terms.وُسِّطَ: was cut in the middle / divided

ai.seo_question: Which part of a severed body receives the funeral prayer if the heart is present in only one half?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in funeral prayers by identifying the heart as the vital center of life; thus, the presence of the heart in one half signifies that the majority of the person's essence remains there. This ruling is particularly significant in cases of fragmented remains, such as those devoured by wild animals, ensuring the prayer is not unnecessarily duplicated or omitted. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the heart as the locus of the soul's connection to the body for ritual purposes.

en.hubeali:
Sahl, from Abdullah Bin Al Husayn, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
'When the man is cut in the middle into two halves, Salaat would be prayed upon that in which is the heart’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from abu al-Jawza’ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from ‘Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his ancestors who has said the following: “’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about a man who was burnt. He (the Imam) instructed them to pour water on him well, then perform Salah (prayer) for the deceased.’”
